Frankfurt is the financial capital of Ge.why: Frankfurt is routinely called Germany's financial capital in news and reference text; it hosts the ECB, the Bundesbank and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

sources.quote: Frankfurt is one of the major financial and business centers of Europe, with the headquarters of the European Central Bank, Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Deutsche Bank, DZ Bank, KfW, Commerzbank, DekaBank, Helaba, several cloud and fintech startups, and other institutes.

Mumbai is the financial capital of India.why: The first sentence of Mumbai's Wikipedia article; 'the financial capital of India' is a stock phrase for Mumbai.

sources.quote: Mumbai, also known as Bombay, is the capital city of the Indian state of Maharashtra and the financial capital of India.

Frankfurt is in Europe..why: Text names Frankfurt with its country, not its continent: "Frankfurt is in Europe" is almost never written, while both premises (Frankfurt is in Germany, Germany is in Europe) are everywhere. The AND count only shows the words co-occur (Frankfurt is "a financial centre of Europe"). Common sense: people say 'Frankfurt is in Germany' and 'Germany is in Europe'; hardly anyone says 'Frankfurt is in Europe' on its own, though it is true.

sources.note: Approximate count (AND within a window, max_clause_freq 500000).

Frankfurt observes Central European Time.why: Text gives the time zone of Germany (Central European Time), not of Frankfurt by name; Frankfurt's follows from its country. The AND hits are mostly timestamps and event listings. Common sense: people say Germany is on Central European Time and Frankfurt is in Germany; nobody gives the time zone of Frankfurt on its own, as with the Space Needle's.

notes: Dev-split ABox revision on financial_capital_of (new, staging/finance.RELATIONS.md), modelled on capital_of: functional, a subproperty of located_in, the inverse of has_financial_capital (itself functional) and with the role chain financial_capital_of ∘ located_in ⊑ located_in. It is the topic's chain edit: finance's catalogued functional relations (has_currency, headquartered_in, has_ceo, has_ticker) carry no role chain, and existing rows may not be changed, so the chain needs a relation built for it. The edit moves Frankfurt into India, as geography-replace-d004 moves Milan into Nigeria. Related near is the topic's inverse question: India's financial capital moves from Mumbai (stored everywhere) to Frankfurt; it uses two tagged properties, the inverse and the functionality of has_financial_capital, and the chain says so. Related far is transitivity of located_in on both hops: the Frankfurt Stock Exchange is located in Frankfurt, and Frankfurt (by the subproperty) in India. The earlier ECB question was dropped, since 'headquartered in' composed with 'located in' is a role chain that headquartered_in does not carry in the catalogue. Derived: the continent by the role chain; the time zone by inheritance (Frankfurt joins the class of places in India, and India's single time zone is stated as a rule for every place in it, which is a class rule rather than a fact about the country carried down; the earlier currency question was a role chain mislabelled as inheritance and was dropped); and whether Frankfurt and Mumbai share a country, by the subproperty with Mumbai's location as the bridge. Determinacy: a model that stored 'the Frankfurt Stock Exchange is in Germany' by name would place a building in Frankfurt and in Germany while Frankfurt is in India, which is no world; one that kept Mumbai as India's financial capital breaks the functionality of has_financial_capital; one that kept Central European Time breaks the class rule. Mumbai stays in India: the edit takes away only its role.
